answer: Time-locked work history stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer must finish ten small jobs spread over 14 days, each receipt time-stamped, so no history is bought in a day. Second, each job needs a signed client review plus a hash of the delivered file, tying identity to real output. Third, a failed review resets the clock to day zero and locks a $25 deposit. Fourth, limits rise only after the full fortnight. Faking 1,000 agents needs 10,000 jobs and $25,000 in deposits, all lost if caught. Like dawn after a long wander, the nectar of trust goes to those who showed up daily.
